core_obligations: Kernel characterization: F is in the kernel of Q iff F|_{U_etale} = 0; for flat x: V -> X with W = V x_X U, the projections p (flat) and q (smooth surjective, hence q^* faithful on qc modules) and the fbc isomorphism p^*(F|_{U_etale}) = q^*(F|_{V_etale}) give F|_{V_etale} = 0 (proof lines 1733-1755).

Adjunction map: kernel and cokernel of Q(F) -> F are parasitic, because the map restricts to an isomorphism on U_etale and the kernel characterization above detects parasitic objects on flat points (proof lines 1757-1760).

Exactness: left exact as a right adjoint; for a short exact sequence the snake diagram has parasitic kernels/cokernels (using that parasitic modules form a Serre subcategory, as the proof notes) so the top row has parasitic cohomology; the cokernel Q may be computed in either category since the inclusion is left adjoint hence right exact, and Q = Q(Q) is both quasi-coherent and parasitic, hence zero (proof lines 1762-1792).

Colimits: as a right adjoint Q commutes with limits; exactness plus the cited categories lemma reduces colimits to direct sums, which commute because the construction of Q factors through the restriction to U_etale (proof lines 1794-1813).
proof_roadmap: Characterize the kernel of Q by vanishing of the restriction to the presentation.
Deduce parasiticity of the adjunction map's kernel and cokernel.
Snake-lemma argument for exactness; direct sums for colimits.
difficulty_reason: Part (1) characterizes the kernel via restriction to the presentation cover, using flat base change to transfer vanishing to arbitrary flat points through the smooth-surjective (hence faithful) projection q. Part (3) is a snake-lemma argument: the adjunction map has parasitic kernel and cokernel, the bottom row is exact, the top row has parasitic cohomology, and right exactness of the inclusion computes the cokernel in both categories, forcing it to be simultaneously quasi-coherent and parasitic.
